page: Microsoft Azure M32-8ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Cache architecture comprises 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 105 MB L3 cache. It includes instruction set support for AVX and AVX-512 foundation, alongside standard cryptographic AES instructions. Hardware resources are paired with 875.0 GB of system memory, delivering 109.38 GB of RAM per vCPU, and accompanied by 1100 GB of local SSD storage. No dedicated graphics accelerators are included.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate that the configuration prioritizes massive memory capacity over raw processing throughput. With 8 vCPUs, computational scores remain low relative to cloud-wide benchmarks, recording a PassMark CPU score of 6371.07, a single-core Geekbench score of 895.0, and a multi-core score of 3456.0. Memory throughput evaluates at 38.73 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 31.04 GB/sec for writes. Workload processing benchmarks show 5.28 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, 5.77 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and 4.6 tokens per second during LLM text generation with a 7B parameter model.

The primary operational tradeoff of the M32-8ms is the extreme ratio of memory to compute. Organizations paying for the expansive 875.0 GB memory footprint receive modest processor throughput limited to 8 vCPUs. Cost efficiency is optimized strictly for workloads that require immense in-memory data structures but exhibit low CPU intensity. Suitable use cases include large in-memory databases, SAP HANA development or non-production deployments, caching layers, and analytical workloads constrained by dataset size rather than core count.
description: Microsoft Azure M32-8ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for workloads requiring massive random-access memory relative to CPU resources. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280M processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, supported by 105 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 extensions. The platform integrates an exceptional 875.0 GB of RAM alongside 1100 GB of local SSD storage, without GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show modest compute and integer performance, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 3456.0 and 5.28 million Redis SET operations per second, reflecting the system design trade-off where compute allocation is constrained to 8 threads. The instance delivers high resource density for memory-bound applications, making it well fitted for in-memory databases, large caching clusters, and data processing architectures where memory volume takes priority over thread parallelism.
